passages.title: The station clock
passages.body: When the railway closed, the station clock stopped at 6:17. For years Lena passed it every morning. After the council voted to convert the building into a market, a contractor offered to install a new clock. Lena instead asked him to repair the old one. On opening day she heard it strike seven and instinctively quickened her step, though she had nowhere she needed to be.

passages.title: Shading a model pond
passages.body: Students placed identical containers outdoors with equal volumes of water. They varied only the percentage of the surface covered by an opaque screen. Each container started at 20 °C. Temperatures below were measured after 90 minutes.

passages.title: Two maps of a city
passages.body: Map A shows every bus stop at equal scale. A visitor can use it to locate the stop nearest a museum, but tracing a route across the crowded downtown is difficult. Map B enlarges downtown and compresses the outskirts. Its designer argues that the map should clarify transfers even if the distance between symbols no longer reflects the distance between stops.

passages.title: A neighborhood archive
passages.body: [1] The team planned to scan the neighborhood's oldest photographs. [2] It borrowed a scanner from a nearby school. [3] Its first few files were too large to upload over the library's connection. [4] A volunteer changed the export settings, and the uploads went through. [5] By Friday the team had posted forty photographs.

items: Where should the writer place the sentence “The team had expected scanning to be the hardest part.” to best introduce an unexpected obstacle?
After sentence 2, the reader knows the scanning plan and equipment. Sentence 3 then directly contradicts the expectation by introducing a problem with uploading.
Which revision of sentence 4 correctly joins the two independent clauses?
A volunteer changed the export settings the uploads went through.
A volunteer changed the export settings; the uploads went through.
A volunteer changed the export settings, the uploads went through.
A volunteer changed; the export settings and the uploads went through.
Both clauses can stand as sentences. A semicolon joins them directly. A comma alone creates a comma splice.
Which replacement for “too large to upload over the library’s connection” in sentence 3 most precisely explains why the uploads failed?
too large to finish uploading before the connection timed out
much bigger in quite a few ways
The time-out explains how file size interacted with the connection. The other choices describe size or difficulty without identifying the practical consequence.
A box holds 5 green tokens and 3 yellow tokens. If two tokens are drawn without replacement, what is the probability they are different colors?
Either green then yellow or yellow then green works. Add (5/8)(3/7) and (3/8)(5/7) to get 30/56 = 15/28.
A workshop can rent a lathe for USD 18 per hour or pay USD 42 for a pass plus USD 11 per hour. For whole hours only, what is the least rental length for which the pass is strictly cheaper?
Solve 42 + 11h < 18h. Then 42 < 7h, so h > 6. At six hours the costs are equal. Seven is the least whole hour that works.
The middle terms cancel. The remaining expression is $9-4i^2=9+4=13$.
For real x, let $f(x)=x^2-4x+7$. Which number is the least possible value of $f(x)$?
Complete the square to get $(x-2)^2+3$. The square is nonnegative and equals zero at x = 2, giving minimum 3.
A circle has center $(2,-1)$ and passes through $(5,3)$. What is its area?
The squared radius is $3^2+4^2=25$. Multiply by pi to get the area.
What does Lena's reaction to the repaired clock most strongly suggest?
She expects the railway to reopen.
The clock brings an old routine back to mind.
She thinks the clock shows the wrong time.
She plans to leave the market immediately.
She quickens her step automatically despite having no appointment. That physical reaction suggests a habit associated with the clock.
How does the opening detail about 6:17 help structure the passage?
It sets up a contrast with the clock striking seven at the end.
It shows why customers prefer shopping before seven.
It explains the contractor’s reluctance to repair the clock.
It proves the clock had never kept time accurately.
The fixed opening time presents a stopped clock. The chime at the end demonstrates that it runs again.
What trade-off does Map B make?
It leaves out museum stops to show longer routes.
It preserves physical distances at the expense of transfer clarity.
It distorts visual distances to make transfer points clearer.
It shrinks downtown to make space for the outskirts.
Map B enlarges downtown and compresses the outskirts, so locations are shifted to improve usability for transfers.
How much warmer was the completely unshaded container than the container with 50% shade after 90 minutes?
The unshaded container reached 29 °C, compared with 24 °C at 50% shade. The difference is 5 °C.
Why did each container start at the same temperature?
To keep starting temperature from complicating comparisons
To prove every container warmed at a constant rate
To ensure all containers ended at the same temperature
To eliminate the need for a 0% shade comparison
Holding the starting temperature fixed makes final-temperature differences easier to attribute to the shade treatment.
One student predicts a constant temperature drop for each additional 25 percentage points of shade. Another predicts that the drop varies. Which observation directly favors the second prediction?
The first step reduced temperature by 2 °C and the next by 3 °C.
Constant drops would be equal across equal changes in shade. The first two drops are 2 and 3 °C, which differ.
Which choice completes the sentence with a clear modifier? “Walking through the greenhouse, ______.”
the sound of sprinklers reached Jo
Jo noticed pale orchids near the door
there were several orchids in bloom
The subject immediately after the introductory modifier should identify who was walking. Jo is the walker.
The previous sentence explains that the trail bridge closed for repairs. Which opening best signals the consequence in “______, hikers had to use the longer route”?
The closure caused the detour. As a result signals cause and effect.
Which revision preserves the complete meaning of “The committee postponed the vote until a later time because several members were absent” most concisely?
The committee voted after several members arrived.
With several absent, the vote was scheduled.
The committee postponed the vote because several members were absent.
The committee postponed the vote until later because some people were absent.
Postponed already indicates a later time. The correct revision also retains who decided, what changed, and the cause.
A printer charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant price per poster. Eight posters cost USD 34 and twelve cost USD 46. What is the setup fee?
Four additional posters cost USD 12, so each costs USD 3. Subtract USD 24 from the eight-poster total to find the USD 10 fixed fee.
Squaring the target yields $x^2+2+1/x^2=25$. The target is positive, so its value is 5.
A cone and a cylinder have equal radii and equal volumes. How does the cone’s height compare with the cylinder’s height?
It is three times as large.
A cone has volume equal to a third of its base area times height. With equal bases and volumes, its height must be triple.

A baker marked every batch with the temperature at which the dough rose. Over time she found that the best loaves came from batches left near a drafty window, which she had thought too cold. Which idea best captures the passage?
Tracking results challenged the baker's assumption.
The baker discovered how to heat the kitchen evenly.
The baker suspected the window was warmer than the oven.
Tracking ingredients revealed a problem with the flour.
The recorded results contradict the baker's initial belief about the drafty window. No information about ingredients or even heating appears.

At the meeting Niko opened a binder of complaints. As residents described a footpath that flooded after each storm, he flipped past his prepared speech and drew a small map. What can most reasonably be inferred?
Niko had seen the path flood before.
Niko intended to close the path permanently.
Niko adjusted his response to what he heard.
Niko had written a speech about that exact path.
He sets aside the prepared speech and draws a map while listening to specific reports, suggesting he adapts his response.
“The director gave the volunteers latitude in arranging their shifts, as long as someone staffed the desk.” In context, what does “latitude” mean?
The volunteers can arrange their own shifts within one constraint, so latitude means freedom to decide.
Which sentence correctly signals that there is exactly one project coordinator?
The project coordinator Mira Chen will open the meeting.
The project coordinator, Mira Chen, will open the meeting.
The project coordinator Mira Chen, will open the meeting.
The project coordinator, Mira Chen will open the meeting.
The title alone identifies the coordinator. The name supplies nonessential information and requires a pair of commas.
Five measurements have a mean of 12. A sixth measurement raises the mean to 14. What is the sixth measurement?
The first five sum to 60. The six sum to 84, so the new measurement is 24.

“The first pottery shards remained damp under the shelter. When a volunteer placed other shards on a raised mesh tray beneath the same shelter, they dried by morning.” Which detail best supports airflow as an explanation?
The first objects were pottery shards.
Both groups were beneath the same shelter.
The drier shards rested on raised mesh.
The volunteer checked the second group in the morning.
A raised mesh surface enables air to reach the underside. Its association with faster drying supports the explanation directly.
